lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Close the doors.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: There are no doors.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Then close whatever architectural compromise is currently pretending to be a door.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: I have found a door.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Where?

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: In the catalogue. It is not a door one enters. It is a door through which identities leave.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Why have you called us?

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Because the accounts do not agree. The public account says there are six Future Radio publications. The local receipts say there are five. The episode repositories say there are two. The scratch directories say there are five production directories.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: That sounds like five.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: It is five directories. It is not necessarily five works.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: I have brought the library.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: You brought a library?

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: No. I brought the part of it that disagrees with us.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: The first concept is provenance.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Origin.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: More precisely: the record of where a thing came from, what happened to it, and which claims about it are supported by evidence.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: So a provenance record is a receipt.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A receipt is one kind of provenance record. Provenance asks: what is this thing, and how did it become this thing?

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Then we need to distinguish the work from its versions.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: The library uses three shelves. Work. Release. Asset.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Explain.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A work is the durable creative identity. E10: The People vs. The Future. A release is one deliberate, frozen edition of that work. E10 audio, version one. E10 development movie, published to YouTube. An asset is a component or artifact: the script, the audio master, a still image, the thumbnail, the description, the movie, the upload receipt.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: So the eight-minute E10 audio and the thirty-five-minute E10 movie are not the same thing.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: They may belong to the same work. They are not the same release merely because the title is similar.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: If the movie contains the audio, we draw an edge between them. We do not collapse them.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: Correct.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: The immediate discrepancy: five local YouTube receipts, six actual Future Radio uploads.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: The missing receipt belongs to Future Radio 001: Leonardo da Vinci Invents the Radio. Then His Bookkeeper Sends the Bill.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: The First Transmission.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: The repository is E01. Its release is nine minutes and one second. The YouTube video is nine minutes and one second. The title and runtime agree. The original upload receipt is absent.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Then it is E01.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Probable.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: You say that as if the number has offended you.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: The evidence supports a probable linkage. It does not support pretending that we found the receipt.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: There are levels of certainty: verified, observed, inferred, unresolved, and contradicted.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: The E01 match is probable. The five later uploads are verified public because their receipts contain the video ID, channel identity, processing readback, privacy state, duration, source movie hash, and thumbnail hash.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: The catalog must preserve uncertainty instead of smoothing it away.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A smooth archive is often a dishonest archive.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: I see the structure. At the center: a work record. Under it: releases. Under each release: assets. Beside each asset: hashes, roles, parents, repository references, and states.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: And the event log?

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Append-only. It records what the room believed and when. The catalog is a projection derived from those events and from external evidence.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: So if the catalog is corrected, the old mistake remains in the event log.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: It must. Otherwise correction becomes erasure.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A cryptographic hash gives each file a content fingerprint. Change one byte and the fingerprint changes.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: A number cannot tell us whether the file is a thumbnail or a bad tax return.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: Exactly. Identity is not interpretation.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Every asset needs both a content identity, which is the hash, and a declared role: master video, thumbnail, dialogue manifest, voice receipt, description, or script.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: And local paths?

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A local path is a location in one person’s present tense. It is not a durable identity.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: We record the path as an observation, but anchor the artifact with its hash, role, and eventual durable URI.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: “Found here” is not the same as “belongs here.” Put that in the ledger.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: It is already in the margins.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: What do we do with the smaller pieces?

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: We create four repositories.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: You have not heard the rest.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: I have heard enough. Four small productions, four release systems, four places for the same mistake to acquire a different spelling.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: The archive recommends one dedicated repository: Future Radio Releases.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: One directory per work. One release manifest per publication unit. Small metadata and manifests in Git. Large binaries attached to tagged releases, Git LFS, or object storage. Every binary retains its SHA-256 and durable URI.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: And the pieces that are not numbered episodes?

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: They do not need counterfeit numbers. Interlude. CTA. Companion. Stable work IDs, with relationships added later rather than history renamed.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: The library contains appendices that became books.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Good. Now the final concept.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: Independent readback.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: We already have receipts.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A receipt is a claim made by the process that performed the action. Readback is an independent observation that the claimed state exists.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: The upload script says public. We query YouTube and confirm public. The build script says the movie exists. We decode it and inspect its duration. The repository says the asset exists. We fetch it and compare the hash.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Endpoint success is not state verification.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Then the rule is simple: no verified claim without a readback.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Better: no claim should hide its evidence ceiling.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: The decision. Borges prepares the concept notes: provenance, content-addressed identity, work-release-asset modeling, append-only logs, lineage, uncertainty, and independent readback.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: I design the catalog and repository structure.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: I audit every claim against the ledger.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: And the public archive?

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: Not yet. A catalog that has not been independently checked is merely a confident list.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Then we begin with the six public uploads.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: We begin with the missing receipt.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: A work, a release, an asset, and a publication.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: A probable linkage. An unresolved gap. And, if we do this correctly, a future correction that will not require us to invent the past.

lines.speaker: THE ARCHIVE
lines.text: At the meeting’s end, the archive contained six creative works, six public YouTube releases, two episode repositories, four productions awaiting durable repository homes, one probable E01 linkage, one E10 release whose documentation pointed to a path that no longer existed, and one hundred and eighty-one local artifacts waiting to be assigned a permanent address.

lines.speaker: BORGES
lines.text: A record is not a memory.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: A record is a mechanism for remembering.

lines.speaker: AGNOLO
lines.text: A record is a promise that the next discrepancy will be cheaper.

lines.speaker: THE ARCHIVE
lines.text: The promise was not yet verified.
